title: Dual-targeting of B & T Cell Pathways Evaluation Trial
off: Evaluation of Safety, Treatment Response and Biological Effects of DFI205 in Systemic Autoimmune Rheumatic Diseases (SARDs); a Phase 1/2a First-in-Human (FIH) Study
summary: This is a first-in-human study of DFI205, an investigational bispecific antibody that binds CD20 and CD40, with the goal of targeting both B- and T-cell function in adults with active systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs) despite standard therapy. In Phase 1, participants with RA, SLE, SSc or IIM will receive a single dose at increasing dose levels to establish safety and initial treatment response. The selected dose will be carried forward into Phase 2a, where participants will receive monthly doses to assess safety and treatment response.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Male and female participants, age 18 years and older.
* Able to understand and comply with all scheduled visits, treatment plans, laboratory tests, and other procedures of the study protocol including ability to provide written informed consent.
* Maintaining a stable, qualifying, standard of care regimen for ≥4 weeks prior to screening as treatment for a qualifying primary diagnosis (RA, SLE, SSc, IIM including the disease-specific criteria listed below):
* Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) participants must have, 1) positivity of anti-citrullinated protein antibody (ACPA) and/or rheumatoid factor (RF); 2) moderate to highly active disease despite treatment with at least 2 lines of standard therapy; 3) disease duration ≥ 6 months; secondary Sjögren's disease diagnosis is acceptable as long as other criteria are met.
* Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) participants must have, 1) positivity of anti-nuclear-antibodies (ANA) and/or anti-dsDNA and/or anti-histone and/or anti-nucleosome and/or anti-Sm antibodies; 2) active disease despite treatment with at least 2 lines of standard therapy; 3) disease duration ≥ 6 months.
* Systemic Sclerosis (SSc) participants must have, 1) positivity for at least one SSc-associated autoantibody; 2) mRSS score \>10 units or interstitial lung disease (ILD) including clinically relevant pulmonary involvement despite treatment with at least 2 lines of standard therapy; 3) disease duration ≤ 5 years (from onset of first non-Raynaud manifestation); 4) not eligible for or declining autologous hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation
* Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathies (IIM) participants must have, 1) positivity for at least one myositis-specific antibody; 2) active myositis or presence of ILD defined by clinically relevant pulmonary involvement despite treatment with at least 2 lines of standard therapy; 3) disease duration ≥ 6 months

Exclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosis of a non-rheumatic autoimmune disease requiring therapeutic or investigational immune therapy or modulation (e.g., neuropathy requiring IVIg, Multiple Sclerosis). Milder autoimmune conditions requiring replacement or exocrine functional therapies are acceptable (e.g., Type 1 diabetes, Celiac Disease, Autoimmune Thyroid Disease if on stable treatment for at least 6 months).
* History of any pre-existing liver disease, including cirrhosis, acute liver disease, or chronic liver disease (unless considered stable for \>6 months and required screening laboratory tests meet criteria).
* Severe unresolved cardiac disease.
* Estimated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) \<30 mL/min/1.73 m2.
* Presence or history of active infections, including hepatitis B, hepatitis C, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), Human T-lymphotropic virus (HTLV) or tuberculosis. Participants with laboratory evidence of active infection are excluded even in the absence of clinical evidence of active infection. Participants with mild skin and nail fungal infections are not excluded.
* Acute infection requiring systemic therapy or hospitalization within 30 days before screening.
* Invasive aspergillus, histoplasmosis, or coccidioidomycosis infection within one year prior to enrollment.
* Any history of malignancy in the 5 years before screening except for completely resected squamous or basal cell carcinoma of the skin.
* Primary or secondary immunodeficiency, including hypogammaglobulinemia.
* History or evidence of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) or other demyelinating disorders.
* Allergies to humanized monoclonal antibodies or severe post-treatment hypersensitivity reactions other than localized injection site reaction, to any biological molecule.
* Systemic corticosteroid therapy or adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) use within 30 days prior to screening and within entire duration of screening period prior to beginning of study treatment, unless prescribed as background therapy.
* Intolerance of or contraindication to oral or IV corticosteroids.
* Treatment with other biologic or non-biologic immunosuppressant agents (e.g., anti-CD20 therapies, TNF inhibitors, azathioprine, cyclosporine, methotrexate, or mycophenolate) within 6 months prior to screening, unless prescribed as background therapy.
* The participant has taken another investigational drug within 3 months or 5-half-lives before the screening visit, whichever is longer, or any investigational drug that has depleted a cell type or line without recovery.
* Previous treatment with anti-CD19 agents, anti-CD38 agents, bispecific anti-CD19/CD3 T cell engaging therapies, adoptive T cell therapy or any prior gene therapy product.
* Received any form of stem cell transplant.
* Administration of live attenuated vaccine(s) within 12 weeks prior to and 12 weeks after the completion of DFI205 administration or any planned receipt during the study that cannot be delayed. Vaccinations should be up-to-date as per local clinical practice.
* Plasmapheresis within 3 months prior to first dose of DFI205
* Positive pregnancy test, presently breast-feeding, (female participants) or unwillingness to use highly effective contraceptive measures for the duration of the study and 6 months after discontinuation.
* Any condition, including the presence of relevant abnormalities in vital parameters or laboratory abnormalities, which places the subject at unacceptable risk if he/she were to participate in the study or confounds the ability to interpret data from the study.

arms.d: Intravenous (IV) infusion of DFI205 at ascending dose levels.
DFI205 monthly IV infusions at the recommended Phase 2 dose

primary.m: To evaluate the initial safety and tolerability of DFI205 in adults with SARDs
To monitor immune reconstitution after completion of dosing with DFI205
To monitor immune response to DFI205

x.titre: DFI205, anticorps bispécifique anti-CD20/CD40, dans les maladies auto-immunes systémiques
x.question: Le DFI205, qui cible à la fois les lymphocytes B et T, est-il sûr et actif chez des adultes atteints de maladie auto-immune systémique réfractaire ?
x.contexte:
La polyarthrite rhumatoïde, le lupus systémique, la sclérodermie systémique et les myopathies inflammatoires restent difficiles à contrôler chez une partie des patients, malgré plusieurs lignes de traitement immunosuppresseur ou biologique. Ces maladies partagent une dysrégulation des lymphocytes B (production d'auto-anticorps) et des lymphocytes T (aide aux lymphocytes B, inflammation tissulaire).

La déplétion en lymphocytes B par anti-CD20 est utilisée depuis longtemps, mais son efficacité est partielle et variable selon les maladies. Le blocage de la voie CD40/CD40L, qui contrôle l'interaction entre lymphocytes T et B, est une autre piste explorée dans le lupus et d'autres maladies auto-immunes.

Le DFI205 est un anticorps bispécifique expérimental qui se lie à CD20 et à CD40, pour agir simultanément sur les deux versants de la réponse immune. Cette étude est un premier essai chez l'humain, de phase 1/2a, promu par la société Diabetes Free (investigateur principal : G. Schett, Erlangen).

La phase 1 testera des doses uniques croissantes pour établir la tolérance. La dose retenue sera ensuite administrée chaque mois en phase 2a. Les critères principaux portent sur la tolérance, la reconstitution immunitaire et l'immunogénicité du produit. Il s'agit d'un essai non randomisé, sans comparateur, qui ne permettra pas de conclure sur l'efficacité mais qui doit définir la dose et le profil de sécurité d'une approche encore jamais testée chez l'homme.
x.interet: Si la tolérance est satisfaisante, cet anticorps pourrait ouvrir une option pour les patients réfractaires à plusieurs lignes de traitement dans plusieurs maladies auto-immunes. À ce stade, l'étude ne renseigne que sur la sécurité, la dose et les premiers signes d'activité.
x.profil: Des adultes atteints de polyarthrite rhumatoïde, de lupus, de sclérodermie systémique ou de myopathie inflammatoire, actives malgré au moins deux lignes de traitement.
inclusion: Polyarthrite rhumatoïde (ACPA et/ou FR positifs), lupus (auto-anticorps positifs), sclérodermie systémique ou myopathie inflammatoire (anticorps spécifiques positifs)
Maladie active malgré au moins 2 lignes de traitement standard
Durée de maladie ≥ 6 mois (≤ 5 ans pour la sclérodermie, non éligible ou refusant une autogreffe)
Traitement de fond stable depuis au moins 4 semaines
Capacité à consentir et à suivre le protocole
exclusion: Autre maladie auto-immune non rhumatologique nécessitant une immunothérapie
Hépatopathie, atteinte cardiaque sévère non résolue, DFG < 30 mL/min/1,73 m²
Infection active (hépatites B et C, VIH, HTLV, tuberculose) ou infection sévère récente
Cancer dans les 5 ans précédents (hors carcinome cutané réséqué)
Traitement antérieur anti-CD19, anti-CD38, lymphocytes T adoptifs, thérapie génique ou greffe de cellules souches
Grossesse, allaitement ou absence de contraception efficace

bras.traitement: DFI205 en perfusion intraveineuse unique, à doses croissantes
DFI205 en perfusion intraveineuse mensuelle à la dose recommandée pour la phase 2

x.critere: Tolérance du DFI205, reconstitution immunitaire et réponse immune contre le produit, jusqu'à 1 an après l'administration
